title: Karnataka Congress MLA submits resignation over elephant relocation row, 2 others threaten to quit

ai.summary: Karnataka Congress MLA Nayana Motamma resigned over alleged state Forest Department plans to relocate elephants from Hassan district to Bhadra Tiger Reserve, citing lack of consultation with MLAs and rising human-animal conflict. Two other Congress MLAs threatened to resign if the operation continues.

facts.claim: Congress MLA Nayana Motamma submitted resignation to Assembly Speaker’s office
facts.quote: Bengaluru: Congress MLA from Karnataka’s Mudigere constituency, Nayana Motamma, submitted her resignation to the Assembly Speaker’s office on Monday, protesting the state Forest Department’s alleged move to drive elephants from neighbouring Hassan district towards the Bhadra Tiger Reserve in Chikkamagaluru district.

facts.claim: Two other Congress MLAs threatened to resign if the department continues with the operation
facts.quote: Two other Congress MLAs—T.D. Rajegowda of Sringeri and H.D. Thammaiah of Chikkamagaluru—have also threatened to resign if the department continues with the operation.

facts.claim: Relocating elephants doesn't work as they remember their paths and walk back
facts.quote: Relocating elephants doesn't work. They remember their paths and walk back. This is their home too.

facts.claim: Karnataka recorded 709 human fatalities due to human-animal conflict between 2011-2025
facts.quote: Government data accessed by ThePrint show that Karnataka recorded 709 human fatalities due to human-animal conflict between 2011-12 and 30 November 2025.

ai.background_note: Karnataka's rising human-animal conflict has led to MLA resignations over elephant relocation plans, with the state accounting for 22.14% of India's elephant population and 709 human fatalities from such conflicts between 2011-2025.
